name: Langford

facts.text: Langford regulates tree cutting on private property under Tree Protection Bylaw No. 2269. In most cases the City needs a certified arborist's report before it issues a Tree Cutting Permit, and it may also ask for a Registered Professional Biologist's report near lakes, streams and sensitive ecosystems.
facts.excerpt: In most cases the City will require a report from a certified arborist before issuing a Tree Cutting Permit.
facts.note: V2: confirmed. The same page also says 'Bylaw No. 2206 protects trees in all areas of Langford' and links an older 'Bylaw No. 2179' file; the November 2024 FAQ and the linked bylaw file are No. 2269, so treat 2269 as current. The 2269 PDF is a scan with no text layer and was not read.

facts.text: Langford's Tree Protection Bylaw applies across the city to any tree at least 20 cm in diameter measured 1.4 m above the base. It also covers trees planted under a development or tree cutting permit, trees on City land, trees protected by a covenant, and trees showing evidence of nesting or use by raptors, osprey or a heron colony.
facts.sourceTitle: Langford Tree Protection Bylaw - Frequently Asked Questions (Nov 2024)
facts.excerpt: A diameter of at least 20cm, measured 1.4m above the base
facts.note: V2: new; closes the R1b threshold gap. This is the FAQ linked from the current Tree Removal page, and it names Bylaw No. 2269, so the 20 cm figure is current, not just a carry-over from the interim bylaws. It lists penalties; CONTRACT: no $ amounts.

facts.text: In Langford, pruning needs no permit when it follows Best Arboriculture Practices, for example not removing more than 25% of a tree's live foliage. Topping is restricted in most circumstances.
facts.sourceTitle: Langford Tree Protection Bylaw - Frequently Asked Questions (Nov 2024)
facts.excerpt: Examples of BAP include not removing more than 25% of the tree’s live foliage and restricts topping of a tree in most circumstances.

facts.text: Langford's tree bylaw exempts cutting a protected tree species that is a regulated invasive plant, or an unregulated invasive plant of concern declared by the Province or the Invasive Species Council of BC.
facts.sourceTitle: Langford Tree Protection Bylaw - Frequently Asked Questions (Nov 2024)
facts.excerpt: Cutting or Removal of a Protected Tree species that is a regulated invasive plant or an unregulated invasive plant of concern in British Columbia
facts.note: V2: new (exemption f in the FAQ).

facts.text: A protected tree removed in Langford must be replaced, with a refundable deposit for each replacement tree: half is returned once the tree is planted and the rest a year later if it is still healthy.
facts.excerpt: If you remove a protected tree, you will be required to replace it.
facts.note: V2: confirmed. Added the deposit-return terms from the same page ('Fifty percent of the deposit will be returned once the tree is planted and the full deposit will be returned a year after planting if the tree is still in good health.'). No replacement ratio is stated. The page gives a per-tree amount; CONTRACT: no $ amounts.

facts.text: Langford's Environmental Protection & Hazard Area development permit guidelines (June 2026) cover riparian zones, sensitive ecosystems, the 200-year floodplain, steep slopes, drainage-concern areas and interface fire hazard areas. Inside an environmental or hazard area, land may not be altered (site clearing, tree or vegetation removal, blasting or landscaping) without a development permit unless an exemption applies.
facts.sourceTitle: Environmental Protection & Hazard Area Development Permit Area Guidelines (City of Langford, June 2026)
facts.excerpt: Land must not be altered (including site clearing, tree/vegetation removal, blasting, and/or landscaping) when it is within an area designated for:
facts.note: V2: confirmed against the PDF. Correction: the guidelines map these areas in OCP Bylaw No. 2200 (Maps 10, 11 and 13-16); 'urban forest' is a theme of the guidelines, not a separate DPA. The Tree Removal page links an older OCP file (official-community-plan-1200.pdf).

facts.text: Langford's riparian development permit area extends 45 m from the high-water mark of every watercourse, mapped or not. Disturbance inside it needs a development permit or an exemption, and the usual minimum setback is 30 m from the high-water mark, backed by a QEP assessment under the provincial riparian regulation.
facts.sourceTitle: Environmental Protection & Hazard Area Development Permit Area Guidelines (City of Langford, June 2026)
facts.excerpt: The DPA is measured as 45m from the high-water mark of a watercourse. Disturbance within this area is prohibited unless authorized by a DP or DP exemption.
facts.note: V2: new; covers the R1b 'Langford Lake / Florence Lake' gap generally (watercourses as RAPR defines them, which include lakes). s.1.6.3, verbatim: '30 m from the high-water mark for all other watercourses' (10 m or 30 m from the top of ravine bank, by ravine width).

facts.text: In Langford's riparian and sensitive-ecosystem permit areas, ecological restoration (planting native vegetation or removing non-native or invasive vegetation with small hand tools) is exempt from a development permit, though the City may ask for a disposal, safety and erosion-control plan.
facts.sourceTitle: Environmental Protection & Hazard Area Development Permit Area Guidelines (City of Langford, June 2026)
facts.excerpt: or removing non-native or invasive vegetation using small hand tools.
facts.note: V2: new (s.1.1.1 e). The same exemption appears for hazard areas (s.2.1.1 e). Machine clearing is not covered by this exemption.

facts.text: Langford maps Interface Fire Hazard development permit areas (Map 16, OCP Bylaw No. 2200). Removing trees or vegetation there is exempt from a development permit only if no other environmental or hazard permit area applies, and lands rated Moderate or Low on the map are exempt.
facts.sourceTitle: Environmental Protection & Hazard Area Development Permit Area Guidelines (City of Langford, June 2026)
facts.excerpt: For the removal of trees or vegetation, if no other Environmental Protection or Hazardous Area Development Permit Areas apply;
facts.note: V2: new (s.2.3.1); partly closes the R1b wildfire-interface gap (Bear Mountain etc. not named).

facts.text: Langford's Community Standards Bylaw No. 2255 (adopted May 19, 2026) defines 'unsightly' to include grass over 30 cm and noxious weeds, and requires owners and occupiers to make reasonable efforts to eradicate noxious weeds on their property, so rental and vacant lots need regular mowing.
facts.sourceTitle: Community Standards Bylaw No. 2255, 2026 (City of Langford)
facts.excerpt: includes the accumulation of Waste or other materials, overgrown grass over 30 centimetres, Noxious Weeds,
facts.note: V2: confirmed (definition of 'Unsightly'; s.8 Noxious Weeds; adoption date on the last page). 'Noxious Weed' takes its meaning from the provincial Weed Control Act. The bylaw repeals the old Unsightly Property and Noxious Weed Control bylaws. 'Rental and vacant lots need regular mowing' is our framing.

facts.text: Langford owners and occupiers must keep the boulevard next to their property free of noxious weeds and waste, with grass mowed to 30 cm or less. They must also keep boulevard landscaping clear of sight lines and watered within CRD watering rules, unless the City waters it.
facts.sourceTitle: Community Standards Bylaw No. 2255, 2026 (City of Langford)
facts.excerpt: keep grass within the Boulevard mowed or trimmed to a height of not more than 30 centimetres;

facts.text: Langford's Community Standards Bylaw counts grading and landscaping as construction. Exterior construction and site preparation or grading are allowed Monday to Friday 7 am-7 pm and Saturday 9 am-5 pm, and not on Sundays or statutory holidays without a Noise Permit. Rock breaking, drilling, crushing and blasting are limited to weekdays 8 am-5 pm.
facts.sourceTitle: Community Standards Bylaw No. 2255, 2026 (City of Langford)
facts.excerpt: Site preparation, grading, or servicing work: (i) Monday to Friday between the hours of 7:00 a.m. and 7:00 p.m. (ii) Saturdays between the hours of 9:00 a.m. and 5:00 p.m.
facts.note: V2: new (s.29). The 'Construction' definition, verbatim, includes 'activities ancillary to that construction, demolition, or reconstruction, such as grading, landscaping, or maintenance'. Owners doing their own home maintenance may work Sundays and holidays 10 am-5 pm (s.29(3)); this does not cover contractors.

facts.text: For new development, Langford requires landscape and irrigation plans for boulevards, parks and other public land to be approved by Parks before work starts (Schedule 14, Subdivision and Development Servicing Bylaw No. 1000). Irrigation plans must come from a certified irrigation designer (IIABC or IA), and topsoil must meet the BCSLA/BCNLA Landscape Standard. Development permit landscape plans also follow Zoning Bylaw No. 300 s.3.21 and the City Landscape Policy.
facts.sourceTitle: Subdivision and Development Servicing Bylaw No. 1000, consolidated to 2024-05-09 (City of Langford)
facts.excerpt: Irrigation plans must be designed by a certified irrigation designer – turf/commercial classification as certified by IIABC or IA.
facts.note: V2: the old 2023-10-26 consolidation URL returns 404; this newer consolidation is linked from the Bylaws Directory. Schedule 14.1.1, verbatim: 'Landscape plans, Irrigation plans and detailed landscape cost estimates must be submitted to Parks and approved prior to commencing landscape work'. Zoning s.3.21(4) confirms Landscape Policy No. 6630-00.

facts.text: Langford's Zoning Bylaw No. 300 says required landscape areas should keep existing trees and native vegetation (other than invasives), and all unbuilt, unparked parts of a lot must be landscaped. In multi-family, commercial, industrial and institutional zones, planted areas need an underground automatic irrigation system. Front-yard fences are limited to 1.2 m, and side and rear fences on houses and townhouses to 1.8 m.
facts.excerpt: All planted areas (trees, shrubs, groundcover, lawn, raised beds and planters in a landscape and screening area must be serviced and maintained by an underground automatic irrigation system.
facts.note: V2: new (s.3.21.01-3.21.03). The file is linked from the Bylaws Directory; its URL says 20240415 but page footers read '20 Jul 26', so check the consolidation date. Fences inside Interface Fire Hazard or Riparian DPAs need a DP or an exemption (s.3.21.03(2)).

facts.text: Langford's public advisories have a dedicated blasting category. In November 2026 it listed current blasting notices for 890 Walfred Road, 721 Treanor Avenue and 3003 Irwin Road (Westhills), so new-build yards near development sites can sit next to active rock work.
facts.excerpt: Find all of the latest blasting, infrastructure, parks and other advisories here.
facts.note: V2: the old source (the Langford Heights advisory) is a June 2024 notice that has expired; the source is now the live advisories list. Correction: removed 'rock is close to the surface across much of Langford', which was our inference and is not a City statement. Specific notices expire, so name them only with a date.

facts.text: In Langford, only individually owned residential lots of 2,023 m2 (0.5 acre) or more may burn, with a permit, in two periods: November 1-30 and March 15-April 15, not on long weekends. Burning runs sunrise to sunset, only leaves and tree trimmings may be burned, piles are limited to 1.5 m by 1.5 m, and land-clearing or construction debris may never be burned.
facts.excerpt: The first is between November 1 and November 30 and the second is between March 15 and April 15 of any calendar year (inclusive).
facts.note: V2: the source is now the City's official Fire Rescue page, replacing the SECONDARY news source. Same page, verbatim: 'Only individually-owned residential properties that are 2023 square meters (0.5 acres) or greater or greater in size.' Fire Regulations Bylaw No. 1532. The permitted months are now confirmed.

gaps: Bylaw 2269 text itself: the linked PDF is an image scan (no text layer), so its sections were confirmed only through the City's Nov 2024 FAQ.
